name: Crucible Industries Forge Rifle FR-9 'Ironmonger'
description:
Crucible Industries built the FR-9 for environments that destroy lesser weapons. The Ironmonger's monolithic steel-ceramic receiver is milled from a single block of composite material, eliminating weak points at joins and seams. It chambers the heavy 7.62mm caseless round and delivers it with a long-stroke gas piston system that cycles reliably through sand, mud, chemical contamination, and temperature extremes from -40C to 65C.

The FR-9 lacks the smart features of its Tessera and Arcturus competitors. There is no BCI link, no targeting AI, no electromagnetic acceleration. What it offers is mechanical perfection — a weapon that fires when the trigger is pulled, every time, in any condition. The iron sights are tritium-illuminated. The magazine is a standard 30-round steel box. The charging handle is oversized for gloved or prosthetic hands.

Crucible markets the Ironmonger to frontier security forces, mining operations, and independent militias who operate beyond reliable maintenance infrastructure. It has become the weapon of choice for operators who distrust networked systems and prefer the certainty of analog reliability.
specifications:
caliber: 7.62mm caseless
effective_range: 600m
rate_of_fire: 650 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 30 rounds
weight: 4.1 kg
tactical_use: The FR-9 is the weapon you bring when nothing else will work. Its heavier caliber provides superior barrier penetration and stopping power compared to intermediate rounds, and its mechanical simplicity means field repairs require basic tools and no diagnostic software. Operators sacrifice smart-link precision for the guarantee that the weapon functions regardless of EMP, jamming, or network compromise.
cultural_context: The Ironmonger has a cult following among anti-corporate frontier communities and old-school operators who view BCI-linked weapons as surveillance tools with triggers. Crucible cultivates this identity deliberately — their marketing emphasizes independence, self-reliance, and freedom from corporate ecosystems. In Tier 1-2 settlements, the FR-9 is often the most advanced weapon available and the most trusted.
story_hooks: A Crucible Industries factory has been producing FR-9s with hidden RFID trackers at the request of a corponation that wants to map militia supply chains.
An FR-9 recovered from a crime scene has serial numbers that trace back to a batch supposedly destroyed in a factory fire — someone faked the destruction records.

Tessera Industries Quantum Entanglement Detonator QED-1 'Certainty'

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist assault rifle with aggressive, angular lines and a distinctly utilitarian silhouette. The monolithic receiver dominates the platform, creating an almost architectural appearance—like industrial machinery weaponized. No curves or ergonomic softening; every surface serves function. The long gas piston tube runs above the barrel in a pronounced ridge. Heavy, purposeful, unmistakably built to endure.
physical_description.dimensions: 965mm overall length, 127mm width at magazine well, 95mm height from rail to charging handle. 558mm barrel length with deep rifling visible at muzzle.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and balanced—4.1kg sits solidly in the shoulder without feeling front-heavy despite the monolithic construction. Hefty enough to command respect, distributed well for sustained fire. The oversized charging handle adds tactile weight to the control interface.
physical_description.primary_material: Monolithic steel-ceramic composite block forms the receiver—a seamless casting with no visible seams or rail bolts. The gas tube and barrel are high-carbon steel. Bolt carrier is hardened steel with visible tool marks from machine finishing.
physical_description.finish: Matte black parkerized coating with visible wear patterns revealing grey steel underneath at edges and charging handle. The composite receiver shows a subtle speckled texture—darker grey with charcoal flecks from the ceramic matrix. Intentionally anti-reflective; no polish or shine anywhere.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Deep matte black with gunmetal grey undertones on the composite receiver. Accents: Bright tritium green in the iron sight posts. Steel grey on exposed machining marks.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressively textured rubberized pistol grip with vertical ribs for bare-handed or gloved purchase. The charging handle is knurled steel with deep grooves sized for prosthetic digits. Oversized magazine well edges provide grab points.
distinctive_features: Monolithic receiver with zero visible fasteners or junction lines
Pronounced long-stroke gas piston tube running the length of the upper receiver
Tritium-illuminated iron sights with witness marks for field zeroing
Oversized charging handle with knurled grip and witness lines
Heavy muzzle brake with four angled ports
Rail-less design—no picatinny; pure mechanical sights only
Steel magazine with witness holes and numbered round counts
Bolt carrier shows deliberate machine tool marks—no polish
Heat vents machined into the gas tube shroud
Field-strip markings engraved along the receiver seam
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industries logo—angular Φ symbol inside a hexagon—stamped on the left side of the receiver. Model designation 'FR-9 IRONMONGER' stamped in sans-serif caps below the logo. Serial number on the right receiver panel. 'GENE-FORGE MFG' stamped on the barrel near the receiver interface. Manufacturing date code etched below the charging handle.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously functional. Parkerize finish shows honest use—scuff marks on the furniture, patina on the composite where hands grip it repeatedly. No rust or corrosion; maintenance is evident despite the battle scars. Some operators customize the furniture with leather wraps or tactical tape, but the core receiver remains unmodified.
